scope.intended_use: research provenance and future reproduction planning
prohibited_inferences: Do not interpret somatic nucleated-patch conductance density as AIS or axonal density.
Do not interpret a fitted single-compartment gbar as a direct experimental measurement.
Do not pool Wilbers 2023 measurements with Eyal 2018 model-estimated compartment densities.
Do not assign either study's values uniformly to all compartments or all human cortical pyramidal subtypes.
Do not infer a dendritic sodium-channel density or back-propagating action-potential mechanism from these somatic recordings.

wilbers_2023.title: Human voltage-gated Na+ and K+ channel properties underlie sustained fast AP signaling
wilbers_2023.data_access_status: DataverseNL released version 3.0 and CC0-1.0 metadata verified (65 files); selected mechanism and Python source bytes downloaded/read and SHA-256 hashed in isolated session; raw numeric workbooks and AP-clamp trace matrix not downloaded; source files not vendored.

cohort.tissue_source: neurosurgical tissue described as healthy cortex removed to access deeper structural pathology
cohort.cell_class: supragranular pyramidal neurons; the study examines L2/L3 pyramidal neurons
cohort.privacy: Study reports anonymized data and written informed consent; no patient-level data are stored here.

experimental_conditions.recording_configuration: somatic nucleated patches for isolated voltage-gated Na+ and K+ current measurements
experimental_conditions.channel_isolation: pharmacological isolation in separate Na+ and K+ experiments

temperature_c.note: The paper states that all channel recordings were at 34 C except sodium-channel kinetics recordings, which were at 25 C.

experimental_conditions.liquid_junction_potential: Table S1 voltage-dependence data are explicitly stated to be uncorrected for a 15 mV liquid-junction potential.

measured_somatic_nucleated_patch_conduct.scope: somatic nucleated-patch membrane; not AIS or axon
measured_somatic_nucleated_patch_conduct.note: The main article reports mean +/- SEM; the thesis appendix Table S3 reports the corresponding means +/- SD. These are somatic patch measurements and should not be promoted into whole-cell or axonal conductance densities.

slope_factors.reason: The thesis Table S1 extraction labels the slope-factor unit as ms^-1, which is dimensionally suspect for a Boltzmann voltage slope. Verify the source files/equations before use.

sodium: Steady-state activation and inactivation curves are shifted toward more depolarized voltages than in mouse.
Activation and inactivation time constants are slower than in mouse at the tested voltages.
Recovery from inactivation is faster than in mouse.
Relative conductance availability at -80 mV is reported as 0.81 +/- 0.16 in human and 0.63 +/- 0.21 in mouse.
potassium: Steady-state activation and inactivation curves are shifted toward more depolarized voltages than in mouse.
K+ currents activate faster in human neurons at lower membrane potentials in the tested protocol.
Fast and slow inactivation components are described; recovery time constants are similar between species, while human currents recover to a larger proportion of initial amplitude.
Relative conductance availability at -80 mV is reported as 0.94 +/- 0.05 in human and 0.86 +/- 0.06 in mouse.
channel_kinetic_findings.model_limit: The authors report that the HH-based model reproduced K+ currents less well than Na+ currents and did not capture every potassium-current property.

single_compartment_hh_model_fit.model_scope: single compartment with 10 um diameter; not a reconstructed L2/3 morphology
single_compartment_hh_model_fit.interpretation: Model-derived maximal conductances used in the paper's single-compartment AP simulations. The authors explicitly note that the sodium density required by the single-compartment AP model exceeds the density measured in somatic nucleated patches.

source_notes: The study analyzes human supragranular pyramidal neurons and somatic voltage-gated channel properties.
Somatic nucleated-patch recordings do not provide AIS-specific or axonal channel-density measurements.
The article's data files are listed under DataverseNL DOI 10.34894/L5J0SD, but the raw files have not yet been obtained and verified by AMSN.
DataverseNL version 3.0 is released under CC0-1.0 and contains 65 files; a curated file inventory with official SHA-1 and selected source SHA-256 values is stored in the AMSN research references.
The human Na/K MOD mechanisms and fitting scripts were inspected and hashed; they have not yet been compiled or reproduced in NEURON.
The human K fitting script has an unresolved mismatch between its intermediate inactivation-fit values and later final-best-fit dictionary.
Both canonical MOD files contain a source-level trap0 branch/limit inconsistency; its impact on compiled NEURON execution has not yet been measured.

eyal_2018.title: Human Cortical Pyramidal Neurons: From Spines to Spikes via Models
eyal_2018.fitting_method: multi-objective optimization against recorded somatic/axonal spike waveforms
eyal_2018.critical_assumption: The study assumed ion-channel kinetics similar to rodents; these are model estimates, not direct compartment-resolved human channel-density measurements.
missing_evidence: No direct human dendritic sodium-channel recordings in the study.
The extent of back-propagating action potentials in human L2/L3 pyramidal dendrites remains unknown in the article.
source_notes: The article models six human L2/L3 pyramidal cells using approximately 900 recorded spikes.
Kv3.1 and persistent potassium estimates are separate model components and are not directly equivalent to the total somatic voltage-gated potassium current measured by Wilbers et al. 2023.
ModelDB archive 238347 remains not downloaded or reproduced in AMSN in the current checkpoint.
